title: Finite Newton correction from scalar polynomial identities with separated parameter torsion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $t\in R$, and let $c\geq0$ be an integer such that every $z\in t^cR$ satisfying $t^mz=0$ for some integer $m\geq0$ is zero. Let $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ with $d\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and let $J\subseteq P$ be an ideal. Its square $J^2$ consists of finite sums of products of two elements of $J$. Suppose $G\in P$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_d\in J$ satisfy $$Gf-\sum_{i=1}^d(\partial f/\partial x_i)g_i\in J^2\qquad(f\in J),$$ where the partial derivatives are those of [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Let $h,q\geq0$ be integers with $q>2h$ and $q-h\geq c$. If $a\in R^d$ satisfies $G(a)=t^h$ and $f(a)\in t^qR$ for all $f\in J$, then there exists $a^+\in R^d$ such that $a_i^+-a_i\in t^{q-h}R$ for every $i$ and $f(a^+)\in t^{2(q-h)}R$ for all $f\in J$. Polynomial evaluation is substitution of the coordinates of $a$. No Noetherianity, completeness or non-zero-divisor hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Elkik, I, Lemma 1, printed pp.555–558, especially the torsion intersection condition and Taylor-correction argument on pp.556–557; agent adaptation using the scalar conormal identities of Gabber–Ramero (5.4.4), printed pp.148–149. No Stacks tag states this evaluated-scalar torsion variant. Both archival sources WANTED; read online 2026-10-24.

proof.text: Put $s=q-h$. Then $q=h+s$, $s>h\geq0$, and $s\geq c$. Since each $g_i\in J$, choose $u_i\in R$ with $g_i(a)=t^qu_i$. Set $v_i=t^su_i$ and $a_i^+=a_i-v_i$. Thus $t^hv_i=g_i(a)$ and $a_i^+-a_i=-v_i\in t^sR$. These choices depend only on the fixed $g_i$ and $a$, and will be used for every $f\in J$.

source.place: I, Lemma 1, printed p.557: write the correction as a quotient of an element in t^qR; finite scalar-identity adaptation

proof.text: Fix $f\in J$ and write $D_i=(\partial f/\partial x_i)(a)$ and $L_f=f(a)-\sum_iD_iv_i$. Evaluation is the ring homomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. An element of $J^2$ is a finite sum $\sum_k b_kc_k$ with $b_k,c_k\in J$; write $b_k(a)=t^q\beta_k$ and $c_k(a)=t^q\gamma_k$. Its evaluation is therefore $t^{2q}\sum_k\beta_k\gamma_k$. Apply this to $Gf-\sum_i(\partial f/\partial x_i)g_i\in J^2$ and use $G(a)=t^h$ and Step 1. For some $w_f\in R$ we obtain $$t^hL_f=t^hf(a)-\sum_iD_ig_i(a)=t^{2q}w_f.$$

source.place: (5.4.4), printed p.148: scalar factorization modulo J^2; direct evaluation of the assumed polynomial identities

proof.text: Define $z_f=L_f-t^{2q-h}w_f$. Since $h\leq q$, Step 2 gives $t^hz_f=0$. Also $f(a)\in t^qR\subseteq t^sR$ and every $v_i\in t^sR$, so $L_f\in t^sR$. As $2q-h\geq s$, also $t^{2q-h}w_f\in t^sR$. Hence $z_f\in t^sR\subseteq t^cR$. The given torsion hypothesis, applied with $m=h$, forces $z_f=0$. Thus $$L_f=t^{2q-h}w_f\in t^{2s}R,$$ because $2q-h=2s+h$. This uses the torsion hypothesis on the deep difference $z_f$, rather than cancelling $t^h$ in $R$.

source.place: I, Lemma 1, printed p.557, torsion intersection argument following equation (4); explicit deep-difference calculation

proof.text: For a monomial $r\prod_i x_i^{e_i}$, expand $r\prod_i(a_i-v_i)^{e_i}$ by multiplying its finitely many factors. The term containing no $v_i$ is its value at $a$. The terms containing exactly one $v_i$ sum to $-\sum_{i:e_i>0} e_i r\,a_i^{e_i-1}\prod_{j\ne i}a_j^{e_j}v_i$, which is $-\sum_i(\partial f/\partial x_i)(a)v_i$ for this monomial, by [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. Each remaining term contains at least two $v$ factors and belongs to $t^{2s}R$. Summing over the finite monomial expansion of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] yields $f(a^+)-L_f\in t^{2s}R$. Step 3 now gives $f(a^+)\in t^{2s}R=t^{2(q-h)}R$ for every $f\in J$, proving the claim. For $d=0$ the tuple and sums are empty, the remainder is zero, and Steps 2 and 3 still apply.

lean.statement: theorem exists_newton_correction_of_torsion_separated {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (t : R) (c : ℕ) (htorsion : ∀ z : R, t ^ c ∣ z → (∃ m : ℕ, t ^ m * z = 0) → z = 0) (d : ℕ) (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin d) R)) (G : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R) (g : Fin d → MvPolynomial (Fin d) R) (hg : ∀ i : Fin d, g i ∈ J) (hidentity : ∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R, f ∈ J → G * f - ∑ i : Fin d, pderiv i f * g i ∈ J ^ 2) (h q : ℕ) (hq : 2 * h < q) (hc : c ≤ q - h) (a : Fin d → R) (hG : aeval a G = t ^ h) (ha : ∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R, f ∈ J → t ^ q ∣ aeval a f) : ∃ a' : Fin d → R, (∀ i : Fin d, t ^ (q - h) ∣ a' i - a i) ∧ ∀ f : MvPolynomial (Fin d) R, f ∈ J → t ^ (2 * (q - h)) ∣ aeval a' f
